key_insight: When importance sampling is regularized in off-policy policy gradients, the usual reward-shift invariance breaks, and covariance-based estimators restore it by centering the reward-score product.
engineering_relevance: For RL post-training of large language models, the choice of baseline and score centering affects bias and variance, especially under clipped or truncated importance ratios.
method: Reformulate the policy gradient as a covariance between reward and importance-weighted score.
Use a group-mean baseline to center rewards with a sample mean.
Use score centering to subtract the population mean score; its utility depends on whether importance sampling is sequence-level or token-level.
evidence_signal: The abstract provides a theoretical comparison of sequence-level versus token-level importance sampling and shows how regularized ratios change unbiasedness and variance properties.
watch_item: With token-level importance sampling, using a group-mean baseline alone can introduce bias unless score centering is also applied.
paper_title: Baselines and Score Centering in Policy Gradient Estimation
